subject: Proof-of-Value metrics & ops owners — HyperGrid trial
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@hypergrid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proof-of-Value metrics & ops owners — HyperGrid trial

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed set of measurable success metrics, ownership, and next steps so we can lock the POV scope. I left the technical details lighter here; Ben will follow up with the test harness plan.

Top-level success buckets (proposal)
- Quality (primary): human-eval pass rate >= 90% across the core 12 intent slices; hallucination incidents <= 1.5% on sampled responses. Use the provided evaluation prompts (attached) and blind human raters.
- Latency (SLOs): median (p50) generation latency <= 120ms; 95th percentile (p95) <= 350ms for common 512-token requests under baseline load.
- Throughput: sustain 8 requests/sec (RPS) steady-state per model instance; support bursts to 20 RPS for 5–10 minute windows without > 2x tail-latency degradation.
- Cost: effective cost per 1k tokens (inference + infra) target <= $0.60, measured over the 3-week POV window.
- Operational: end-to-end failure rate < 0.5% (timeouts/errors) and no data leakage incidents.

Measurement approach
- Duration: 3-week POV (rolling 7-day burn for metrics, final snapshot week 3).
- Datasets: canonical prompts (attached) + a 500-sample production replay set you provide.
- Tooling: we'll run continuous telemetry from the Redwood console (token-level cost, latency traces) and produce a daily digest.

Owners (proposed)
- Customer success lead: Claire Nguyen (HyperGrid) — acceptance sign-off for quality deliverable.
- Technical owner (Redwood): Ben Carter — test harness, scoring scripts, infra config.
- Program owner (Redwood): Hannah Schmitt — timeline, escalation, and billing/terms.

Immediate next steps
1) I’ll share a POV success matrix (attached) with exact measurement definitions and sample sizes.
2) Ben to send the eval harness and sample runbook by 6/24.
3) Kickoff verification run the week of 6/29; full POV runs 7/6–7/24.

Attachments: POV_success_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval_prompts_v1.txt (prompt set)

Thanks — if the targets above look reasonable, I’ll lock the kickoff calendar invite and Ben will follow up with the technical checklist.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference (https://redwood.ai)
From: Claire Nguyen <claire@hypergrid.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proof-of-Value metrics & ops owners — HyperGrid trial

Thanks, Hannah — this is great and very close to what we discussed. A few clarifying items so we can confirm internally before kickoff: 

1) Cost model: when you say $0.60 / 1k tokens, is that Redwood-hosted inference with the quantization/throughput profile you expect? Can you include the assumptions (GPU type, quantization) so we can map to our unit economics?
2) Quality dataset: we’ll provide a 500-sample replay set by Friday (6/26). For the human evals, can Redwood provide the rubric and an example of the blinded rating rubric?
3) Peak SLA: during our weekday morning peak (PST 9–11am) we need a baseline of 12 RPS sustained for 15 minutes. Can the throughput target above be raised as a spike SLA for that window?

Assuming those clarifications are straightforward, we’re happy to move forward. Proposed timeline: kickoff verification 6/29, POV run 7/6–7/24, acceptance window 7/27–7/30. 

—Claire
Claire Nguyen
Head of Product, HyperGrid AI
claire@hypergrid.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 15:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proof-of-Value metrics & ops owners — HyperGrid trial

Thanks — quick internal notes / what I’ll deliver by 6/24: 
- Eval harness: a dockerized scoring job + README. Will include the blinded rater rubric and the exact sample size math.
- Infra assumptions: NVidia A10x2 equivalent; we’ll test with int8 quantization first, then run a float16/FP32 control. Cost target $0.60 / 1k tokens assumes int8 with batching and KV prefix cache. I’ll include a sensitivity table (tokens / batch / QPS).
- Telemetry: I’ll enable p50/p95 token-level traces and a daily performance digest to the HubSpot deal link.
- Ops handoffs: I can own the scoring scripts and initial runs. Need platform permission from HyperGrid to ingest the 500-sample replay set (S3 link or Drive share).

Ben (cc to Claire on the plan)
